messages.reasoning_content:
Looking at the error in cell 5:

```
TypeError: only integer scalar arrays can be converted to a scalar index
```

The issue is in this code:
```python
plt.title(class_names[labels[i]])
```

The problem is that `labels[i]` is a one-hot encoded array (because `label_mode='categorical'` was used in the dataset creation), not a single integer. When you try to use it as an index `class_names[labels[i]]`, it fails because you can't index a list with an array.

To fix this, we need to get the class index from the one-hot encoded label. We can use `np.argmax(labels[i])` or `tf.argmax(labels[i])` to get the index of the maximum value (which will be the class index).

Let me fix cell 5:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 10))
for images, labels in train_ds.take(1):
  for i in range(6):
    ax = plt.subplot(3, 3, i + 1)
    plt.imshow(images[i].numpy().astype("uint8"))
    plt.title(class_names[np.argmax(labels[i])])
    plt.axis("off")
```

This should fix the error. The `np.argmax(labels[i])` will return the index of the highest value in the one-hot encoded label array, which is the class index we need.
